prospective_prediction_rows.prospective_prediction_class: route-local prospective prediction / temporal holdout denominator
prospective_prediction_rows.prediction_or_forecast_object: Prospective claim, forecast, temporal holdout, announced target, pre-data discriminator, public prediction, or metadata-only prediction invoked by FAMILYC-EW-CODE.
prospective_prediction_rows.temporal_order_test: Declare the claim timestamp, public registration surface, data-freeze boundary, embargo/unblinding status, forecast horizon, known-at-claim-time information set, and whether the target record was already observed or accessible.
prospective_prediction_rows.postdiction_or_retrofit_risk: Prediction rows must track hindsight, implicit target selection, narrative retrofitting, archive revision backfill, stale public records, and selected-success retelling risks.
prospective_prediction_rows.residual_gap: A true prospective prediction can still be too broad, nonsevere, underdetermined, insensitive to rival candidates, or downstream of a simulator/benchmark rather than a public physical record.
prospective_prediction_rows.forbidden_inference: Do not infer route promotion, public-record closure, candidate identity, or ToE support from prospective wording, forecast timing, or temporal holdout status alone.

prospective_prediction_rows.prediction_or_forecast_object: Archive release timestamp, manifest, changelog entry, or generated summary; not a scientific prospective prediction.
prospective_prediction_rows.temporal_order_test: Package timestamp can support custody only; it cannot prove that a route claim was made before a public physical record existed.
prospective_prediction_rows.postdiction_or_retrofit_risk: Release metadata can hide retrospective edits if not checked against manifest/receipt/navigation freshness.
prospective_prediction_rows.residual_gap: A fresh package can still contain only retrospective or exploratory support.
prospective_prediction_rows.forbidden_inference: Do not infer prediction, forecast success, severity, or route support from archive metadata.
